title: Participle clauses
use_hint: Fix the sentence · Enter = check · Enter = next
note: B2 grammar unit, drafted 2026-09-05 on the home lane, replacing the empty shell. 28 items, inside the 24-40 band. Sits directly after b2_relative_clauses_advanced and is built as its continuation: the first block is literally the REDUCTION of the relative clauses that unit teaches — *who is sitting* -> *sitting*, *which was written* -> *written* — so the recap is structural rather than a card. The teaching spine is the ACTIVE/PASSIVE choice, which is the thing learners get wrong: the man does the sitting so it is -ing, but the book did not write itself so it is the past participle. Every one of the twelve explanations says which way round it is and why, in those terms. The second block moves to adverbial participles — *Feeling tired, she went to bed* and *Having finished the work, he went home* — including the negative position (*Not knowing*) and the Having + past participle form for an earlier action, whose distractor *Having finish* is a real learner error. THE DANGLING PARTICIPLE gets two of the six Use items, because it is the failure that makes participle clauses dangerous rather than merely wrong: *Feeling tired, the bed was very welcome* is grammatical-looking nonsense, and no gate would ever catch it. B11 respected: every gap carries its lemma cue. No gap_class — participles are verb forms, not grammar words, same reasoning as b2_suffixes_1 and b2_reported_speech_advanced. A8 accepts generated as a contraction closure.

cards.title: Participle clauses
points: A participle clause is a **shorter** way to say what you already know.
It drops the relative pronoun and the verb *be*.
**-ing** if the noun does the action; **past participle** if it does not.

rows: the book which **was written** by Orwell

cards.title: You already know
points: Relative clauses 1, 2 and 3 built the long form.
These clauses only shorten it. Nothing new is being said.

cards.title: Which form
points: Ask one question: does the noun **do** the action, or is it **done to**?
This is the same active/passive choice as Passives 2, in a shorter shape.

cards.title: Starting a sentence
points: **-ing** for the same time or a reason.

rows: **Living** in Prague, she knows it well.
**Not knowing** the city, we took a taxi.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: The last two are the dangerous ones: the sentence looks fine and means something silly.

rows: ~~Not knowing the city, a taxi was taken~~
Not knowing the city, **we** took a taxi

items.en: The man sitting over there is my boss.
items.cz: Ten muž, co sedí támhle, je můj šéf.
items.gap: The man ____ over there is my boss. (sit)
accepts: The man sitting over there is my boss.
items.explanation: *who is sitting* shortens to **sitting**. The man does the sitting, so it is **-ing**.
items.explanation_cz: *who is sitting* se zkrátí na **sitting**. Ten muž sedí, proto **-ing**.

items.en: The book written by Orwell is famous.
items.cz: Ta kniha, kterou napsal Orwell, je slavná.
items.gap: The book ____ by Orwell is famous. (write)
accepts: The book written by Orwell is famous.
items.explanation: *which was written* shortens to **written**. The book did not write, so it is the past participle.
items.explanation_cz: *which was written* se zkrátí na **written**. Kniha nepsala, proto příčestí minulé.

items.en: The people waiting at the door look cold.
items.cz: Lidé, co čekají u dveří, vypadají prochladle.
items.gap: The people ____ at the door look cold. (wait)
accepts: The people waiting at the door look cold.
items.explanation: *who are waiting* becomes **waiting** — they do it themselves.
items.explanation_cz: *who are waiting* se stane **waiting** — dělají to sami.

items.en: Anyone wanting a ticket should come early.
items.cz: Kdo chce lístek, měl by přijít brzy.
items.gap: Anyone ____ a ticket should come early. (want)
accepts: Anyone wanting a ticket should come early.
items.explanation: *who wants* becomes **wanting**, even from a simple present.
items.explanation_cz: *who wants* se stane **wanting**, i z prostého přítomného času.

items.en: The money stolen from the shop was found.
items.cz: Peníze ukradené z obchodu se našly.
items.gap: The money ____ from the shop was found. (steal)
accepts: The money stolen from the shop was found.
items.explanation: *which was stolen* becomes **stolen**. Money cannot steal.
items.explanation_cz: *which was stolen* se stane **stolen**. Peníze nemůžou krást.

items.en: The letters sent last week arrived today.
items.cz: Dopisy poslané minulý týden dorazily dnes.
items.gap: The letters ____ last week arrived today. (send)
accepts: The letters sent last week arrived today.
items.explanation: *which were sent* becomes **sent** — the letters were acted on.
items.explanation_cz: *which were sent* se stane **sent** — s dopisy se něco dělalo.

items.en: The woman living above us is a doctor.
items.cz: Žena, co bydlí nad námi, je lékařka.
items.gap: The woman ____ above us is a doctor. (live)
accepts: The woman living above us is a doctor.
items.explanation: *who lives* becomes **living**. She does the living.
items.explanation_cz: *who lives* se stane **living**. Bydlí ona sama.

items.en: The questions asked at the meeting were hard.
items.cz: Otázky položené na schůzi byly těžké.
items.gap: The questions ____ at the meeting were hard. (ask)
accepts: The questions asked at the meeting were hard.
items.explanation: *which were asked* becomes **asked**. Questions do not ask.
items.explanation_cz: *which were asked* se stane **asked**. Otázky se neptají.

items.en: A car parked here will be moved.
items.cz: Auto zaparkované tady bude odtaženo.
items.gap: A car ____ here will be moved. (park)
accepts: A car parked here will be moved.
items.explanation: *which is parked* becomes **parked** — somebody parked it.
items.explanation_cz: *which is parked* se stane **parked** — někdo ho zaparkoval.

items.en: Students studying medicine need six years.
items.cz: Studenti, kteří studují medicínu, potřebují šest let.
items.gap: Students ____ medicine need six years. (study)
accepts: Students studying medicine need six years.
items.explanation: *who study* becomes **studying**. They do it.
items.explanation_cz: *who study* se stane **studying**. Dělají to oni.

items.en: The information given to us was wrong.
items.cz: Informace, které nám dali, byly špatné.
items.gap: The information ____ to us was wrong. (give)
accepts: The information given to us was wrong.
items.explanation: *which was given* becomes **given**. Irregular participle: *given*, not *gave*.
items.explanation_cz: *which was given* se stane **given**. Nepravidelné příčestí: *given*, ne *gave*.

items.en: People arriving late will not get seats.
items.cz: Lidé přicházející pozdě nedostanou místa.
items.gap: People ____ late will not get seats. (arrive)
accepts: People arriving late won't get seats.
People arriving late will not get seats.
items.explanation: *who arrive* becomes **arriving** — they arrive themselves.
items.explanation_cz: *who arrive* se stane **arriving** — přicházejí sami.

items.en: Feeling tired, she went to bed early.
items.cz: Protože byla unavená, šla brzy spát.
items.gap: ____ tired, she went to bed early. (feel)
accepts: Feeling tired, she went to bed early.
items.explanation: *Because she felt tired* shortens to **Feeling**. Same person in both halves.
items.explanation_cz: *Because she felt tired* se zkrátí na **Feeling**. V obou půlkách stejná osoba.

items.en: Having finished the work, he went home.
items.cz: Když dodělal práci, šel domů.
items.gap: ____ the work, he went home. (finish)
accepts: Having finished the work, he went home.
items.explanation: For an action **before** the main one: **Having** + past participle.
items.explanation_cz: Pro děj **před** hlavním: **Having** + příčestí minulé.

items.en: Not knowing the city, we took a taxi.
items.cz: Protože jsme město neznali, vzali jsme taxi.
items.gap: ____ the city, we took a taxi. (know)
accepts: Not knowing the city, we took a taxi.
items.explanation: The negative goes **first**: *Not knowing*.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor jde **první**: *Not knowing*.

items.en: Arriving at the station, I saw my train leaving.
items.cz: Když jsem přijel na nádraží, viděl jsem odjíždět svůj vlak.
items.gap: ____ at the station, I saw my train leaving. (arrive)
accepts: Arriving at the station, I saw my train leaving.
items.explanation: Two things at almost the same moment: **Arriving**.
items.explanation_cz: Dvě věci skoro v jednom okamžiku: **Arriving**.

items.en: Having read the letter, she called her sister.
items.cz: Když si přečetla ten dopis, zavolala sestře.
items.gap: ____ the letter, she called her sister. (read)
accepts: Having read the letter, she called her sister.
items.explanation: The reading came first, so **Having read**.
items.explanation_cz: Čtení bylo dřív, proto **Having read**.

items.en: Working all night, they finished the report.
items.cz: Tím, že pracovali celou noc, tu zprávu dodělali.
items.gap: ____ all night, they finished the report. (work)
accepts: Working all night, they finished the report.
items.explanation: **Working** — the two actions run together.
items.explanation_cz: **Working** — oba děje běží spolu.

items.en: Having lost his keys, he waited in the car.
items.cz: Protože ztratil klíče, čekal v autě.
items.gap: ____ his keys, he waited in the car. (lose)
accepts: Having lost his keys, he waited in the car.
items.explanation: Losing them happened first: **Having lost**.
items.explanation_cz: Ztráta byla dřív: **Having lost**.

items.en: Living in Prague, she knows the city well.
items.cz: Protože žije v Praze, zná to město dobře.
items.gap: ____ in Prague, she knows the city well. (live)
accepts: Living in Prague, she knows the city well.
items.explanation: **Living** — a state that explains the second half.
items.explanation_cz: **Living** — stav, který vysvětluje druhou půlku.

items.en: Having seen the film before, I stayed at home.
items.cz: Protože jsem ten film už viděl, zůstal jsem doma.
items.gap: ____ the film before, I stayed at home. (see)
accepts: Having seen the film before, I stayed at home.
items.explanation: **Having seen** — irregular participle, and the seeing came first.
items.explanation_cz: **Having seen** — nepravidelné příčestí a vidění bylo dřív.

items.en: Opening the door, he found nobody there.
items.cz: Když otevřel dveře, nikoho tam nenašel.
items.gap: ____ the door, he found nobody there. (open)
accepts: Opening the door, he found nobody there.
items.explanation: **Opening** — one action leads straight into the next.
items.explanation_cz: **Opening** — jeden děj vede rovnou do druhého.

items.en: The man sitting over there is my boss.
items.cz: Ten muž, co sedí támhle, je můj šéf.
items.wrong: The man sat over there is my boss.
accepts: The man sitting over there is my boss.
items.explanation: The man does the sitting, so it is **sitting**, not *sat*.
items.explanation_cz: Ten muž sedí, takže **sitting**, ne *sat*.

items.en: The book written by Orwell is famous.
items.cz: Ta kniha, kterou napsal Orwell, je slavná.
items.wrong: The book writing by Orwell is famous.
accepts: The book written by Orwell is famous.
items.explanation: The book did not write anything. Use the past participle: **written**.
items.explanation_cz: Kniha nic nenapsala. Použij příčestí minulé: **written**.

items.en: Having finished the work, he went home.
items.cz: Když dodělal práci, šel domů.
items.wrong: Having finish the work, he went home.
accepts: Having finished the work, he went home.
items.explanation: After *Having* comes the past participle: **Having finished**.
items.explanation_cz: Po *Having* následuje příčestí minulé: **Having finished**.

items.en: Feeling tired, she went to bed early.
items.cz: Protože byla unavená, šla brzy spát.
items.wrong: Feeling tired, the bed was very welcome.
accepts: Feeling tired, she went to bed early.
items.explanation: The person who feels tired must be the subject of the second half. **She** went to bed — a bed cannot feel tired.
items.explanation_cz: Ta osoba, která je unavená, musí být podmětem druhé půlky. **She** went to bed — postel unavená být nemůže.

items.en: The money stolen from the shop was found.
items.cz: Peníze ukradené z obchodu se našly.
items.wrong: The money stealing from the shop was found.
accepts: The money stolen from the shop was found.
items.explanation: Money cannot steal. The past participle is **stolen**.
items.explanation_cz: Peníze krást nemůžou. Příčestí minulé je **stolen**.

items.en: Not knowing the city, we took a taxi.
items.cz: Protože jsme město neznali, vzali jsme taxi.
items.wrong: Not knowing the city, a taxi was taken.
accepts: Not knowing the city, we took a taxi.
items.explanation: **We** did not know the city, so **we** must take the taxi. A taxi does not know a city.
items.explanation_cz: Město jsme neznali **my**, takže taxi musíme vzít **my**. Taxi město nezná.
